writeup: TIC 419143879 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.7507 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 2.39% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 95.1 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location, showing a peak signal-to-noise of 16.9, though the centroid offset of 4.6 arcsec warrants attention. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate for this system. The automated machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.49, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary rather than an artifact. This candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
